zona.snc.efecto.0: Space radiation: damage to the central nervous system, with cognitive impairment, reduced motor function and behavioral changes.
zona.snc.efecto.1: Isolation and confinement: decline in mood, cognition, morale and crew interaction.
zona.snc.efecto.2: Sleep: a small, noisy environment, a longer Martian day and prolonged stress can disrupt it.
zona.snc.anat.organos: Space radiation can damage the central nervous system: cognitive impairment, reduced motor function and behavioral changes.
zona.snc.anat.hueso: The helmet and suit offer protection, but beyond the magnetosphere radiation remains one of the main hazards.
zona.resp.efecto.0: The spacecraft is a closed environment that recycles its air, including the crew's CO₂.
zona.resp.efecto.1: That is why air quality is monitored continuously.
zona.resp.efecto.2: Hypoxia: an HRP catalog risk that is tracked here through oxygen saturation (team mapping).
zona.resp.anat.organos: Cabin air is recycled and its quality is monitored around the clock; hypoxia is one of the risks in the HRP catalog.
zona.cardio.efecto.0: Space radiation: higher risk of cardiac and circulatory disease.
zona.cardio.efecto.1: Altered gravity (weightlessness in transit and 3/8 g on Mars): strains the cardiovascular system, as well as muscles and bones.
zona.cardio.anat.organos: Radiation raises the risk of cardiac and circulatory disease; altered gravity also strains the heart.
zona.metab.efecto.0: Closed environments: stress hormones rise and the immune system is altered, with greater susceptibility to allergies, illness and infections.
zona.metab.efecto.1: No fresh food or variety: monotony and possible nutritional deficiencies.
zona.metab.efecto.2: Radiation: nausea, vomiting, anorexia and fatigue.
zona.metab.anat.organos: In closed environments stress hormones rise and the immune system is altered; without fresh food there is a risk of nutritional deficiencies.
zona.brazos.efecto.1: Sensorimotor adaptation problems: hand-eye coordination and fine motor skills.
zona.brazos.anat.musculo: Altered gravity affects muscles: it is part of the muscle loss that NASA HRP studies with exercise protocols.
zona.brazos.anat.hueso: Without the load of gravity, bone mineral density decreases (it does not increase).
zona.piernas.efecto.0: Bone mineral density drops by about 1 % per month in microgravity according to the NASA HRP video; the gravity page indicates 1 % to 1.5 %.
zona.piernas.efecto.1: Locomotion and balance are affected every time the gravitational field changes (1 g, weightlessness, 3/8 g on Mars).
zona.piernas.anat.musculo: Legs support the body at 1 g; in weightlessness they stop doing so and muscle weakens. Exercise is the countermeasure NASA is studying.
zona.piernas.anat.hueso: Weight-bearing bones, such as those in the legs, are the most affected when gravity is absent.
